questions.question: Name the five steps of the design process and describe, in one sentence each, what a designer does in that step.
questions.expected_answer: Investigate: find out about the problem, the people, existing solutions and available materials, ending with a design brief. Design: sketch several possible solutions and choose the best against the requirements, producing a clear drawing and a materials list. Make: build the product safely and accurately, planning the order of work. Evaluate: test the product against the brief and specifications and record what works and what should change. Communicate: record, label and explain the work throughout and present the solution at the end.

questions.question: Using either the squashed sandwich or the leaking roof example, show how the process looped back instead of running in a straight line.
questions.expected_answer: In the sandwich example, Thabo evaluated his tin after a week and found it rattled, a problem the brief had not mentioned, so he returned to design and make to add a paper pad. In the roof example, Mrs Dlamini evaluated after the next rain, found two more rusting nails, and returned to investigate and make to treat them. In both cases the evaluate step sent the designer back to an earlier step, which is why IDMEC is drawn as a cycle and described as iterative.

questions.question: Explain why communication is treated as running through the whole process, and why it matters for the Practical Assessment Task.
questions.expected_answer: Communication includes keeping notes, writing the design brief, labelling sketches, recording tests and finally presenting the solution. Each step produces a record that others can read and that allows the product to be made or improved by someone else. In the PAT the marks for investigate, design and make are awarded from the written and drawn record, so work that is done but not recorded cannot earn marks.
